name: Lithuania

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary residence)
paths.note: Dividends are taxed at a flat 15% with the foreign withholding credited (up to the treaty rate and the Lithuanian tax); gains on shares, units and interests held more than five years and bought outside an investment account are taxed at a separate flat 15% (GPMĮ art. 6(6)(3)). No wealth tax; children inherit free of tax. A Lithuanian holding company (UAB) is not a path: it would be taxed at 17% a year on a portfolio's gains and most dividends and then again at 15% on payout.

checks.working: Assumes the shares were bought outside an investment account more than five years ago. Gains 150,000 on shares held more than five years: flat 15%, separate from other income (Law on Personal Income Tax art. 6(6)(3); PwC Lithuania Individual - Taxes on personal income) = 22,500. The EUR 500 exemption on financial-instrument gains is ignored. Dividends 200,000: flat 15% (PwC Individual - Income determination) = 30,000; the 15% tax withheld abroad (200,000 x 15% = 30,000) is credited, limited to the Lithuanian PIT on that income and to the treaty rate (PwC Individual - Foreign tax relief and tax treaties), so 30,000 - 30,000 = 0. No wealth tax (PwC Individual - Other taxes). Total 22,500.

Inheritance tax in Lithuania is 5% on a taxable value up to EUR 150,000 and 10% above, but property inherited by a child is not taxed, whatever its value (PwC Lithuania Individual - Other taxes; Law on Inheritance Tax). Each child receives 3,333,333.33 and pays 0. There is no gift tax. A later sale of inherited shares is outside this check.

assumptions: The family are Lithuanian tax residents from arrival (permanent home, or 183 days) and EU citizens needing no permit.

All portfolio shares have been held more than five years before they are sold, so gains bear the flat 15% rather than the progressive 20/25/32% rates. Positions held five years or less, and bonds, are taxed at the progressive rates and would cost more.
Foreign dividends carry 15% withholding, credited in full (treaty rate 15%, same as the Lithuanian rate).
The portfolio is held outside an investment account, because the five-year 15% rule is for shares acquired outside one.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: the investment account (since 2025; PwC: withdrawals above the contributed amount are taxed at a flat 15%; returns reinvested inside are not taxed). Tax arises only on cumulative withdrawals exceeding contributions, so with a EUR 30m contribution and EUR 400,000 withdrawn a year the tax could be deferred for decades; the engine taxes realised gains each year and has no contribution ledger. Conditions (cash-only deposits, a cap on contributions, provider country, single owner) were not verified from the statute.
Whether foreign UCITS ETF units count as 'units' (pajai) for the five-year 15% rule is assumed, not confirmed (see the tax file).
Law on Personal Income Tax and Law on Inheritance Tax texts (e-tar.lt) were not opened; the check relies on PwC (reviewed 1 October 2026) and the KPMG March 2026 newsletter for art. 6(6)(3).

Structures considered and not modelled: a Lithuanian UAB holding company (17% annual company tax; share-gain exemption only for stakes above 10% held two years; dividends then 15% again), never better than direct holding for a diversified portfolio; a private foundation or trust (not researched).
Health insurance (PSD): no contribution on dividends or gains found; a resident with no other insurance basis pays a fixed EUR 80.48 a month (about EUR 966 a year per adult), not modelled.
